Flyout Menu

The mega-menu behind PRODUCTS on ironsoftware.com. Internal as of 2026-08-19 — it is Top Nav’s and nothing else’s, so it is no longer exported on its own; reach for it by giving a nav item a flyout.

7 propsDisclosure, not menuInternal — TopNav onlyPanel from Figma

Preview

The chrome here is still provisional; the PRODUCTS panel below is not. This was built ahead of the Figma frame on purpose — the interaction and accessibility contract is the same whatever the panel looks like, and it is the half that is expensive to get wrong. The generic panel’s padding, radius and shadow are still neutral placeholders. The notch is not: it is Figma’s arrow-flyoutmenu, 19.25×8.7966 with a 2px-radius tip, which is why it is a clipped path and not the rotated square it used to be.

Still opens on click Still opens on focus Escape still closes
Click a trigger, or tab to it and press Enter. Esc closes and hands focus back. Tabbing past the last link closes it. Pressing anywhere outside closes it. Opening one closes the others — two open panels in a nav is always a bug.

The PRODUCTS panel

The panel this exists to open, from Figma FlyoutMenu-product. 1200×376 at the canvas width, rendered by astro-components/internal/ProductFlyout.astro — internal, because it is the content of a panel rather than a control anyone should reach for, the same arrangement Footer’s product row has. Below 594.98px the suite rail drops rather than squashing the products it exists to sell, and the columns fall from three to two to one on their own measured width rather than at a round breakpoint. The three category icons are absent on purpose: Figma sets them in Font Awesome 7 Pro, which cannot ship, so there is nothing correct to draw yet.

Panel hover

Two independent hovers, shown together because a static page cannot capture either. The rail’s scrim goes 40% → 70% — a to bottom gradient under mix-blend-multiply, not a flat black, which is what keeps the stripes reading as stripes instead of flattening toward one grey. A product row takes --color-bg-card-alt across the full column width at --rounded-sm. The CTA’s own hover belongs to Button and is illustrated on its page.

In the bar

Where it actually lives. A Top Nav item with a flyout becomes the trigger, and the panel comes from the slot that names — the panel is the consumer’s content, so a corporate nav bar never has to know ten product names. The trigger is styled to be a .tn-item: same 12px uppercase nav label, same hover, same caret. Measured against a real one, all nine properties match. Open it below.

The panel is 1200px wide and the bar is 1440 with 24 of padding, so at the canvas width it sits inside with room to spare; calc(100vw - 48px) keeps it on screen below that. It is the viewport it has to stay inside, not the trigger’s box — the panel is positioned against the trigger but painted over the page.

It is a disclosure, not a menu

The obvious-looking role="menu" + role="menuitem" is wrong here, and the live site gets this wrong today. That pattern is for application menus — the Cut/Copy/Paste kind — and it makes two promises this component cannot keep.
  • It strips link semantics. menuitem tells assistive tech the contents are commands, so a screen reader stops announcing “link” and stops offering them in its links list.
  • It commits to arrow-key navigation with a roving tabindex, where Tab leaves the whole menu rather than moving through it. Nobody expects that from a site nav.
  • So this follows the WAI-ARIA APG’s Disclosure Navigation pattern instead: a <button> owning aria-expanded and pointing at the panel with aria-controls, ordinary links inside, and Tab walking them in DOM order. Same as Footer Bar’s Free tools panel.

Props

PropWhat it does
labelTrigger text. Required.
openOnHoverAdds hover to click and focus. Off by default — hover is only ever an enhancement.
alignstart / center / end — which edge the panel pins to. A wide panel under a trigger near the right of the bar has to hang left or it leaves the viewport.
notchDraws the pointer up at the trigger.
openRender open on first paint — for docs and tests, not for a live nav.
class
The panel is a slot: whatever you put in it becomes the flyout. Its direct children are numbered by the script and rise in turn as it opens, so composing columns needs no hand-numbering — and a column inserted in the middle cannot leave the sequence stale.
